clue.text: Crazy thief's object of worship

indicators.note: crazy means wild or deranged, so the letters of the next word are jumbled

explanation.surface: A deranged burglar treats his loot as something to worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crazy' is the anagram signal: the six letters of THIEF'S, counting the S, are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A fetish is an object believed to hold magical power and so revered as an idol.

clue.text: Some provide drinks in the jet age

definitions.text: Some provide drinks in the jet age

parts.words: Some provide drinks in the jet age
parts.note: reads like airline drinks service in the era of jet travel, but means water features that shoot jets, some of which are made for drinking from

explanation.surface: Airline cabin crew serve refreshments in the modern era of jet travel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jet age' suggests aircraft; the jets are spouts of water, and drinking ones provide drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: These structures send up jets of water, and the drinking kind supply people with a drink.

clue.text: Magistrate in Rome or a French one in a primitive community

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is placed inside the other here

parts.note: a tribe is a primitive community
un is French for a or one

explanation.surface: A Roman official is likened to a French chief in some primitive society.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Rome an elected officer protecting the plebeians was given this title.

clue.text: Pressman who called on Caesar

parts.note: reads as a journalist visiting the emperor, but means one who pressed a warning on Caesar, telling truth (sooth) about the Ides of March

explanation.surface: A newspaper reporter paid a visit to Julius Caesar for an interview.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's Julius Caesar a seer calls out 'Beware the Ides of March'; 'pressman' plays on pressing a warning, and 'called on' on calling out.
explanation.definitionFit: A seer or prophet foretells events; one famously warned Caesar of his fate.

clue.text: Supporter forms an impression about her

parts.note: an gives the letter A

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece is wrapped round another

parts.note: a dent is an impression in a surface
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fan leaves a mark on a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts HER inside DENT, giving DHERENT after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sticks to a cause or leader is a follower, a backer of it.

clue.text: A reporter on the railways ?

parts.note: reads as a journalist covering the rail beat, but means a fog signal clipped to the track that makes a loud report when a train runs over it

explanation.surface: A journalist covers stories about the railway network.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'report' is also a bang; old railway fog signals exploded on the rails to warn drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a device sets off an explosive charge, and railway fog signals were explosive caps of this kind.

clue.text: By the sound of it, deserve the bird…

indicators.note: this phrase tells us the word is chosen for how it is pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: to earn something is to deserve it

explanation.surface: It seems the bird has earned its reward.
explanation.definitionFit: An erne is a sea eagle, the white-tailed eagle.

clue.text: … zealously imitating another, poor soul

parts.note: following on from the bird in the previous clue, another bird is the emu

indicators.note: poor suggests something damaged or in bad shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A poor soul copies someone else with great eagerness.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots join this clue to 6 down, so 'another' means another bird: EMU. 'poor' scrambles SOUL into LOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being emulous means eagerly trying to equal or outdo someone, keen to rival them.

clue.text: Letter to the old volunteers

parts.note: taken as written
the TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's former reserve force of volunteers

explanation.surface: A letter is sent to former volunteer soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA, the Territorial Army, was the British army's part-time volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Flier embraced by St Ignatius

indicators.note: embraced by says the word sits inside the letters of the saint's name

explanation.surface: An insect is hugged by the saint.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnat is a small flying insect.

clue.text: This fabulous monster described Alice as one

definitions.text: This fabulous monster described Alice as one

parts.words: This fabulous monster described Alice as one
parts.note: in Through the Looking-Glass a horned creature from heraldry calls Alice a 'fabulous monster', turning the tables on her

explanation.surface: A creature of legend calls Alice a monster too.
explanation.walkthrough: In Lewis Carroll's Through the Looking-Glass, the Unicorn says it always thought children were fabulous monsters.
explanation.definitionFit: This one-horned horse of myth is itself a fabulous beast, and in Carroll it gives Alice the same name.

clue.text: Heavyweight certain to have a shaven head

parts.note: a ton is a very heavy weight
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A big man is sure to have his head shaved.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonsure is the shaved crown of a monk or priest.

clue.text: Famous fool's criterion

definitions.meaning: the clown in Shakespeare's As You Like It
a standard by which something is judged

explanation.surface: A celebrated jester's standard of judgment.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare named his jester in As You Like It this, and the word also means a test or benchmark of quality.

clue.text: Fish with a tailpiece

parts.note: the cod is a fish

explanation.surface: A fish served with something on its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A coda is the concluding passage of a piece of music, its closing section.

clue.text: Len goes back into the hold

definitions.text: Len goes back into the hold

parts.words: Len goes back into the hold
parts.note: read backwards, the wrestling grip named in the answer has the letters of the name Len running inside it

explanation.surface: A wrestler named Len returns to grappling.
explanation.walkthrough: Written backwards the answer is NOSLENFLAH, and LEN sits inside it: Len 'goes back' into the hold.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrestling grip where an arm is passed under the opponent's arm and the hand pressed on the back of the neck.

clue.text: But not the country that has Cape Wrath

definitions.text: But not the country that has Cape Wrath

parts.words: But not the country that has Cape Wrath
parts.note: a country with wrath in it is a land of ire; but the real Cape Wrath is at the tip of Scotland, so this is a different nation

explanation.surface: A geography quiz asks which nation lacks the famous headland.
explanation.walkthrough: Cape Wrath is the north-west tip of mainland Scotland. Read as IRE (wrath) + LAND (country), the answer is a country that 'has wrath', though not the one with the cape.
explanation.definitionFit: This island nation west of Great Britain is not where the Scottish headland lies.

clue.text: Brutes did become troubled

indicators.note: become says the letters change into something new, here rearranged

explanation.surface: Thugs grew anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: Disturbed means upset, worried or agitated.

clue.text: Mad son goes in public transport to the bar

indicators.note: goes in says one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: a tram is a form of public transport

indicators.note: mad means crazy, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A crazy young man takes the tram to the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text says 'sod'; the page prints 'son'. 'Mad' makes NSO from SON, which 'goes in' TRAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A transom is a horizontal crossbar, as above a door or window.

clue.text: So good nobody will play such a team?

definitions.text: nobody will play such a team
definitions.meaning: a side no one will take on has no fixtures

explanation.surface: A team so strong that no rival dares face it.
explanation.definitionFit: Without equal describes something peerless, and a side with no fixtures has no games at all.

clue.text: Long letters give point to statements of belief

parts.note: S is south, a compass point
creeds are statements of belief

explanation.surface: Lengthy correspondence sharpens declarations of faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Screeds are long, tedious pieces of writing.

clue.text: Transport may be put in unusual surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings means one piece forms the outside around the other

parts.note: rare means unusual

indicators.note: may be suggests the word could take another form, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A vehicle may be placed in unfamiliar settings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' rearranges PUT into PTU, and RARE is placed round it as its 'surroundings'. 'Transport' is the noun meaning ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: Transport in the sense of overwhelming emotion means ecstasy or delight.

clue.text: Turn back to meditate

definitions.meaning: to throw back light or an image

explanation.surface: Retrace your steps and think things over.
explanation.definitionFit: A mirror throws back an image, and a thoughtful person ponders.

clue.text: Universal recipe prepared for a choosy eater

indicators.note: a dish that is prepared is made up from ingredients, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: A recipe for all, cooked for a fussy diner.
explanation.definitionFit: A gourmet with discriminating taste in food and drink.

clue.text: The low-down on aircraft varnish?

definitions.meaning: a lacquer once applied to the fabric of aircraft wings

explanation.surface: Inside information about the paint used on planes.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for information is the same word as the lacquer used to tauten fabric on early aeroplanes.

clue.text: Order for an architect in Greece ?

definitions.text: Order for an architect in Greece ?

parts.words: Order for an architect in Greece
parts.note: reads as a commission given to a Greek builder, but means one of the classical styles of column

explanation.surface: A Greek architect receives a commission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' is the architectural term for a style of column and entablature, not a request.
explanation.definitionFit: The oldest and plainest of the Greek styles of column.

clue.text: Captain Edward's Friday luncheon

parts.note: Captain Edward Cuttle is a sea captain in Dickens's Dombey and Son, and fish is the traditional Friday meal; his fish is a sea creature

explanation.surface: A naval officer's end-of-week lunch menu.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Edward Cuttle is the old seaman in Dickens's Dombey and Son; Christians traditionally ate fish on Fridays.
explanation.definitionFit: A ten-armed sea mollusc with an internal shell, its name joining the captain's surname to the Friday dish.

clue.text: Sort of print

explanation.surface: A kind of printed material.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text says 'prim'; the page prints 'print'.
explanation.definitionFit: A kind or category, and also the metal characters or lettering used in printing.

clue.text: Service for a large number

explanation.surface: Worship for a big congregation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Catholic Eucharist is called this, and the word also means a great many.

clue.text: Fruit-substitute we hear of from the off-stage crowd

definitions.meaning: a vegetable stalk cooked and eaten as if it were fruit

definitions.text: we hear of from the off-stage crowd
definitions.meaning: the word extras mutter to sound like a crowd talking

explanation.surface: A stand-in for fruit that a theatre crowd murmurs.
explanation.definitionFit: The pink stalks are eaten as a dessert fruit, and actors repeat the word to fake background chatter.

clue.text: Grazing land beyond the river

parts.note: past means beyond
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Fields for cattle lie on the far side of the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text says 'lane'; the page prints 'land'. The Ure is a river in North Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Meadow where livestock feed on grass.

clue.text: Is scared to rewrite Shakespearian role

indicators.note: rewriting the words means their letters are set down in a new order

explanation.surface: An actor is too frightened to revise a Shakespeare part.
explanation.definitionFit: The faithless heroine of Troilus and Cressida is a character in a play by the Bard.

clue.text: If not without a league of nations

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, is a league of nations
less means without, as in 'less tax'

explanation.surface: Unless a league of nations is lacking.
explanation.walkthrough: The page's 'ot' must be 'of': UN is a league of nations.
explanation.definitionFit: Unless means except on condition that, a conditional negative.
